academicJudgment.strongestObjection: A90EC boundary might become an arbitrary generic-method fragment while the specialist ancient Near Eastern academic identity remains absent. UCR has no systematic Egyptian/Mesopotamian chronology, regional language/script history or papyrological/religious-institution sequence. Several supporting courses study later or different regions; openness and candid limitations alone do not make them a meaningful closest response.
academicJudgment.finding: The positive does not rest only on generic skills or removal of difficult credits. This documented core independently includes sustained multi-year ancient historical, textual/material and heritage teaching. UCR contributes actual ancient craft/object cataloguing and drawing, Greek community archaeology, Athenian citizenship/religion with primary/material sources, comparative Persian/Roman imperial history, Gilgamesh/ancient literary and Near Eastern myth interpretation, and substantial colonial collecting/restitution, curatorial and art-historiographic inquiry. These are taught objects and methods that materially respond to the broad route. The later/different-region work supplies specific reception, representation, ownership and research complements, without being relabeled as Near Eastern depth. A narrower honest broad-LAS core claim survives, while whole-degree or specialist equivalence does not. No course-count/EC matching quota is applied.
academicJudgment.adverseTest: Treat unknown25EC as potentially demanding regional/script/research study, and refusal of advanced seminar entry as credible. Those could overturn a complete-degree comparison, so all25unknownEC and35documented choice/advanced/finalEC are unassessed. The independently specified90EC core and real UCR contributions remain. The single philosophy subject is countedonce and unmatched; uncertain year allocation is not used to imply an ordinary valid programme. The30openEC are real but have no assumed contents.

The first-year seminar has an explicit question/source/substantial-paper function in AmericanCentury, with no invented NearEastern topic. Regionalwritten/script/religious/papyrological units remain blank rather than generic-literature/media substitutes. All excluded choice/final/open components remain unmatched. readerValues.programmeDescription: Leiden’s broad Ancient Near Eastern Studies route examines ancient Egypt, the Near East, Greece and Rome through history, religion, archaeology, material culture and written sources. It provides orientation in languages and writing systems alongside museum and heritage study. Specialist ancient-language training belongs to the other tracks.
readerValues.comparisonExplanation: This comparison assesses the documented 90 EC historical, material, textual and heritage core of Leiden’s broad route. UCR can combine ancient archaeology, Athenian society, comparative empires, ancient literature and museum/heritage inquiry in a broader programme. Near Eastern historical depth, language and script history, regional religions and papyrology remain differences. The 10 EC history choice, 10 EC Roman North Africa seminar, 15 EC final work and unidentified 25 EC are excluded from the academic comparison. Genuine 30 EC open study is shown separately; complete degree progression is not certified.

curriculum.limitation: Documented content totals 155 of the nominal 180 EC. Only the specified 90 EC subject and method core is assessed. The 35 EC of documented choice, Roman seminar and final work remain unassessed; the unidentified 25 required EC and full entry/progression remain unresolved. Philosophy counts once for 5 EC, with its year placement unconfirmed. The separate genuine 30 EC open space has no assumed contents.

componentNotes.ono03: First-year students take this seminar alongside History of the Ancient Near East. Its repeated listing does not add a second 5 EC to this partial inventory.
componentNotes.ono04: Counted once for 5 EC. The curriculum lists two versions of the same core course; its correct year allocation remains under review.
componentNotes.ono05: Successful completion is part of the first-year study-advice requirements, together with Written Sources of the Ancient Near East and the language panorama. This is a 10 EC seminar, not extra credit for each repeated reference.
componentNotes.ono06: Successful completion forms part of the route’s first-year study-advice requirements.
componentNotes.ono08: Successful completion forms part of the route’s first-year study-advice requirements.
componentNotes.ono18: Entry requires successful completion of Ancient History and meeting the study-advice threshold.
componentNotes.ono19: One of two approved 10 EC second-year choices. Entry for this route requires Ancient History and the first-year Ancient Near Eastern Studies seminar. Confirmation is still needed that the current seminar meets the applicable thematic-seminar requirement for this cohort.
componentNotes.ono20: The 5 EC thesis seminar requires completion of the first two bachelor years. An exception requires consultation with the study adviser and examination-board permission. Its work supports the separate 10 EC thesis.
componentNotes.ono21: Entry is stated for students who completed the History first year and both second-year History seminars, including one in the same field. Greek and Latin Language and Culture students are also eligible. Ordinary entry from this Ancient Near Eastern Studies route remains unconfirmed.
componentNotes.ono22: The 10 EC thesis requires completion of the first two bachelor years and participation in the thesis seminar. The topic and research approach are agreed with the supervisor, whose appointment requires examination-board approval. The thesis has a maximum of 10,000 words, including footnotes and excluding the bibliography and appendices. Full year-one and year-two completion remains dependent on the curriculum repair.
componentNotes.ono23: 30 EC in the first semester of year three for a minor, approved courses, an approved internship or study abroad. An individual course package needs approval and normally permits at most 10 EC at level 100 and requires at least 10 EC at level 300 or above. Courses must avoid overlap with compulsory study; Honours College courses cannot count. Recognized full 30 EC minors at Leiden, Delft or Erasmus generally need no separate approval. An internship requires prior approval; a placement or study-abroad place is not guaranteed.
